title: Strict tensor comparison for normalized Koszul cones
statement: Let C,J,A,I,b,r,a be arbitrary small-site coefficient and generator-list data [def-sfb-constant-completion-coefficient-data, def-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-system]. Let alpha be a natural strict Koszul-tensor-to-reduction augmentation satisfying the unit and nonzero-Koszul-summand laws [lem-u4-constant-koszul-quotient-augmentation]. Put U=O_b[0]. For every complex P, tensoring the strict cone tower of alpha_U on the left by P yields a strict tower naturally isomorphic to the cone tower of alpha_P. This is an actual strict tower isomorphism before localization. It assumes no Noetherianity, flatness or K-flatness and makes no eventual-vanishing or derived-limit claim.

source.place: Tag 099M, tensoring the finite augmentation; Cohomology on Sites Tags 06YN and 06YP, total tensor and cone signs.

proof.text: Identify the source at U with the actual dual Koszul tower by the total tensor left unitor (and identity-component isomorphism for the reconstructed strict complex). Its degree-zero unit is invertible: identify the dual with the negative Koszul tensor, whose sole degree-zero subset basis is the empty subset and hence the coefficient unit.

At each finite quotient, the sheaf tensor balancing comparison identifies reduction(M) with M tensor the restricted quotient unit. It sends m tensor s to s tensor m. Extend this comparison termwise to complexes and use the single-degree-zero total tensor isomorphism. Associativity and the unitors then give the source and target isomorphisms between tensor by P of the data at U and the data at P. Check compatibility with finite transitions on local pure tensors, where both composites send m tensor s to the image of s tensor m.

The augmentation square is checked on every (p,q) total tensor summand. For q!=0, alpha_P vanishes by its law, while the coefficient augmentation maps to a degree-zero complex and therefore also vanishes in degree q. For q=0 precompose with the isomorphism P^p tensor the degree-zero Koszul unit. Project the ordinary-limit unit law to the finite level: both composites are the actual reduction-unit map on P^p. Cancel the isomorphism and use joint detection by the total tensor inclusions. This proves the square for all P, including unbounded complexes.

Apply the natural signed tensor/mapping-cone comparison to each commuting square. Its shifted-source summand in P-degree p has sign (-1)^p, and its target summand has sign 1; the differential identity is (-1)^(p+1)=-(-1)^p. The same sign on both sides makes each cone transition square commute. Thus the component isomorphisms assemble into the stated strict tower isomorphism.

proof_origin.place: Tag 099M, proof of lemma-naive-completion; finite module and tensor identifications only. Tag 099M, tensoring the finite augmentation; Cohomology on Sites Tags 06YN and 06YP, total tensor and cone signs.

lean.statement:
theorem constantKoszulTensorConeComparison
    (b : Bool) (r : ℕ) (a : Fin r → A)
    (α : ringedKoszulTensorTowerFunctor (coefficients J A I b) r
        (fun i ↦ algebraSection (baseMap J A I b) (a i)) ⟶
      (reductionTower J A I b).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ))
    (hα : KoszulQuotientAugmentationLaws J A I b r a α)
    (P : Cx (coefficients J A I b)) :
    Nonempty
      ((CochainComplex.mappingCone
          (α.app (ringedSiteRingComplex (coefficients J A I b)))).asFunctor ⋙
        tensorLeft P ≅ (CochainComplex.mappingCone (α.app P)).asFunctor)
